question: A Level 2 charger has a maximum output of 32A. The minimum overcurrent device is:
explain_plain: 32 x 1.25 = 40 (625.41 — charging is continuous).

question: A 48A continuous EV charger requires overcurrent protection of at least:
Each outlet installed for EV charging must be supplied by:
choices: A circuit shared with garage lighting
An individual branch circuit with no other outlets
explain_plain: 625.40 in the 2020 NEC — every EV outlet, any size, gets its own circuit.

question: GFCI protection for personnel is required for:
choices: All receptacles installed for EV charging
No EV receptacles — the EVSE handles it
explain_plain: 625.54 covers every receptacle installed for EV charging, in addition to 210.8.

question: EV equipment rated more than 60A or more than 150V to ground requires:
choices: A readily accessible disconnect lockable in the open position
explain_plain: 625.43 with the 110.25 locking rules.

question: Unless listed and marked otherwise, the EV coupling means outdoors is stored at least ___ above grade:
explain_plain: 625.50 — 24 in. outdoors; indoors the figure is 18 in. above the floor.

question: The required receptacle at a permanently installed dwelling pool must be located:
explain_plain: 680.22(A)(1) — not less than 6 ft, not more than 20 ft, max 6 ft 6 in. above the serving surface.

question: All 15/20A, 125V single-phase receptacles within ___ of the pool's inside walls must be GFCI protected:
GFCI protection under 680.21(C) is required for pool motors rated:
choices: 150V or less to ground and 60A or less, single- or three-phase
explain_plain: 680.21(C) — receptacle or direct connection, re-checked against 2020 sources.

question: Pool equipotential bonding conductors are solid copper not smaller than:
explain_plain: 680.26 — 8 AWG solid copper with listed pressure connections.

question: The perimeter bonding ring is installed ___ from the inside walls of the pool:
explain_plain: 680.26(B)(2) — 18–24 in. out, 4–6 in. below subgrade, at least four uniformly spaced attachments; the bonded surface extends 3 ft.

question: Where no bonded part contacts the pool water, the water-bonding surface must be at least:
explain_plain: 680.26(C) — 9 sq in. of approved corrosion-resistant conductive surface.

question: The overhead conductor clearance in any direction from a pool's water level is:
explain_plain: Table 680.9(A) in the 2020 edition (680.9, not 680.8).

question: A pool junction box for an underwater luminaire must be at least ___ from the inside wall of the pool:
explain_plain: 680.24(A) — 4 ft, plus the greater of 4 in. above deck or 8 in. above maximum water level.

question: A wall-mounted underwater luminaire's lens sits at least ___ below normal water level (unless listed for less):
explain_plain: 680.23 — top of the lens at least 18 in. below normal water level.

question: Equipotential bonding under 680.26 does NOT apply to:
explain_plain: 680.30 — storable pools follow Parts I and III; 680.26 is a Part II rule.

question: A spa emergency shutoff (other than at a one-family dwelling) must be at least ___ from the spa:
explain_plain: 680.41 — at least 5 ft away, adjacent, within sight, labeled.

question: Three parallel PV strings each have a module Isc of 10A. The 690.8(A) maximum current is:
Within 30 seconds of rapid shutdown initiation, conductors outside the array boundary must be at or below:
explain_plain: 690.12 — 30V outside the boundary; the boundary is 1 ft from the array.

question: Which is NOT a 690.12 path for conductors inside the array boundary?
choices: A listed PV hazard control system (UL 3741)
An array 8 ft or more from exposed grounded conductive parts with no exposed wiring
Module-level electronics on every other module
explain_plain: 690.12 lists the PVHCS path, the 80V/30-second path, and the separated-array path. Partial module coverage is not one of them.

question: A branch circuit supplying an electric sign must be rated at least ___ and serve no other loads:
explain_plain: 600.5 — 20A minimum, signs/outline lighting only.

question: A fire pump disconnecting means must be capable of being locked in the:
explain_plain: 695.4 — lockable in the closed position, marked in letters at least 1 in. high; the opposite instinct from elevator disconnects (620.51).

question: The 2020 NEC section that governs LED retrofit kits for existing signs is:
explain_plain: 600.35 (new in 2020) — listed kit, instructions, Chapter 3 wiring, damaged parts repaired/replaced, marking per 600.4(B).

question: Selective coordination under 620.62 is triggered where:
choices: More than one driving machine disconnect is supplied by a single feeder
explain_plain: 620.62 — coordination selected by a licensed PE or other qualified person and documented, including device settings.

question: Maximum PV system voltage under 690.7 is calculated using:
choices: Nameplate Voc at 25°C with no correction
Voc corrected to the lowest expected ambient temperature using the manufacturer's temperature coefficient
Vmp times the number of modules
explain_plain: 690.7 (2020) — cold-corrected Voc by the manufacturer's coefficient; dwellings are capped at 600V.

question: DC arc-fault protection under 690.11 is required where PV DC circuits operate at:
choices: 80V or more between any two conductors
explain_plain: 690.11 — listed PV AFCI or equivalent listed components at 80V dc or greater.

question: During fire pump motor starting, voltage at the controller line terminals must not drop more than:
explain_plain: 695.7(A) — 15% starting; 695.7(B) allows 5% running at 115% of full-load current.

question: Copper-clad aluminum (CCA) wire gets its ampacity from which column of Table 310.16?
choices: Its own CCA column printed in the table
The 90°C column, whatever the cable type
explain_plain: CCA sizes like aluminum — rate it in the aluminum column at the cable's temperature limit, then apply the 240.4(D) caps (S-10).

question: A 32A EV charger (40A circuit, per 625.41) is wired in CCA NM cable. The smallest permitted conductor is:
explain_plain: 240.4(D) caps 8 AWG CCA at 30A; a 40A circuit takes 6 AWG CCA — one size up from the 8 AWG copper pick.

question: A pool equipment box holds the same count of 10 AWG THHN conductors, one run in copper and one in CCA. The required box volume is:
choices: The same — 314.16 is figured by conductor size and insulation, not by the metal
Zero, because fill only counts copper
explain_plain: Box fill goes by AWG size and insulation type; the conductor metal never enters the calculation.

question: An EVSE's input lugs are marked 'CU ONLY.' The permitted way to feed it from a CCA branch circuit is:
choices: Land the CCA anyway and torque it tighter
Land the CCA and add antioxidant
Make a listed transition to copper, then land the copper
Backstab the CCA into the lug adapter
explain_plain: 110.3(B) and 110.14: equipment terminals are used as marked and listed. CU-only lugs never take CCA — transition to copper with a listed AL/CU connector first.
